q: 1. Which of the following is not concerned with the authority of Engineers?
options: express an opinion on engineering matter
explain: Divulging confidential matters is a breach of professional duty, not an authority granted to Engineers - engineers are instead obligated to keep client/employer information confidential.

q: 2. Ethics as a normative science needs codes of conduct and guidelines to maintain high level of standard of good behavior in the society. This is applicable to
explain: Ethics as a normative science governing standards of good behavior applies universally to all professions, including lawyers, doctors, and engineers.

q: 3. Engineering profession needs cooperation with the profession of
explain: Engineering projects often require inputs from medical (safety/health), accounting (finance), and legal (contracts) professionals, so cooperation with all these professions is needed.

q: 4. The total number of members in Nepal engineering council is
explain: As per the Nepal Engineering Council Act, 2055, the Council is constituted with a total of 18 members.

q: 5. According to Labour Act, maximum working hour for a labour per week should be
explain: The Nepal Labour Act sets the maximum weekly working hours for a labourer at 48 hours.

q: 6. Workers are not allowed to work continuously more than
explain: As per the Labour Act, a worker must be given a break after continuous work of 5 hours.

q: 7. Which is not concerned with the authority of Engineers?
options: express an opinion of engineering matter
explain: Divulging confidential information is prohibited by professional codes of conduct rather than being an authority of the engineer.

q: 8. Ethics is the science which deals with
explain: Ethics is the science of morals that examines both the rightness and wrongness of professional conduct.

q: 9. Profession is defined as
options: types of service to needy people
explain: A profession is specifically defined as an occupation requiring systematic, specialized knowledge and training, distinguishing it from a general job or occupation.

q: 10. Nepal Engineering Council regulation, 2057 is effective from
explain: The Nepal Engineering Council Regulation, 2057, came into effect on 2057/3/8 B.S., as per NEC records.

q: 11. For the registration of general engineer the amount of fee required is
explain: The registration fee prescribed for a General Engineer under NEC rules is NRs 1,500 (later revised upward to NRs 3,000).

q: 12. The minimum qualification required for a general engineer is
explain: A General Engineer must hold at least a Bachelor's degree in engineering for registration with NEC.

q: 13. The minimum qualification required for a professional engineer is
explain: Registration as a Professional Engineer requires a Master's degree in engineering along with the required experience.

q: 14. The minimum qualification & experience required for the registration of foreigner engineers is
options: bachelor in engineering and 5 years' experience
bachelor in engineering and 10 yrs experience
master in engineering and 5 yrs experience
master in engineering and 10 yrs experience
explain: Foreign engineers must have a Bachelor's degree in engineering with a minimum of 10 years of relevant experience to register in Nepal.

q: 15. The minimum and maximum number of members in the user's committee should be
explain: As per Public Procurement rules, a user's committee should consist of a minimum of 9 and a maximum of 15 members.

q: 16. The employer's have right to
explain: Under procurement law, the employer (as procuring entity) retains the right to either accept or reject any or all bids, subject to prescribed conditions.

q: 17. In any project, Public Work Directives (PWD) accept the following guideline
options: present and past regulation of GoN
explain: Public Work Directives are designed to accommodate donor guidelines, government regulations (past and present), and changes in national law, making it a comprehensive guiding document.

q: 18. The award of contract is given to those bidders whose
explain: Contracts are typically awarded to the lowest evaluated substantially responsive bidder, i.e., the bidder with the lowest bid amount.

q: 19. According to FAR, the project manager has authority to approve the variation upto
explain: Under the FIDIC/FAR-based contract administration norms used in Nepal, the project manager is generally authorized to approve variations up to 10% of the contract value.

q: 20. Who is the Chairperson of Construction Material Rate Fixation Committee?
explain: The Chief District Officer (CDO) chairs the Construction Material Rate Fixation Committee at the district level.

q: 21. For the supply of any goods as per agreement, who is responsible for the all taxed imposed by the GoN
explain: Under standard supply agreements, the supplier bears responsibility for all taxes imposed by the Government of Nepal on the supplied goods.

q: 22. According to Public Work Directives (PWD), applicable rate for the liquidity damage is
explain: PWD prescribes liquidated damages for delay at a rate of 0.1% to 0.5% of the contract price per day of delay, subject to a maximum cap.

q: 23. The user's committee method may be used for labour intensive works with a cost estimate of
explain: The user's committee procurement method is applicable for labour-intensive works with an estimated cost up to NRs 2.5 million.

q: 24. Professional code of conduct issued by Nepal Engineering Council has
explain: The Professional Code of Conduct issued by NEC is organized into 8 articles covering various aspects of professional behavior.

q: 25. Direct purchase can be done when the amount is
explain: Direct purchase (procurement without competitive bidding) is permitted under Public Procurement rules when the estimated amount is less than NRs 0.15 million.

q: 26. Who is the chairperson of central labour advisory board (CLAB)?
options: Director general, department of labour member
explain: The Central Labour Advisory Board (CLAB) is chaired by the Labour Minister (or State Minister for Labour) as per the Labour Act.

q: 27. As per Nepal Engineering Council Act 2055, the tenure of the members of the council is
explain: The NEC Act 2055 prescribes a tenure of 4 years for the members of the Council.

q: 28. Who is the chairperson of Project Coordination Committee?
explain: The Project Coordination Committee at the district level is chaired by the Chairperson of the District Development Committee (DDC).

q: 29. In selecting consultant for procurement goods and service, which of following method adopted?
explain: Consultant selection methods under procurement guidelines include Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS), Fixed Budget Selection, and Least Cost Selection, applied depending on the nature of the assignment.

q: 30. The type of contract when payment shall be made for actual work done at site is
explain: In a Unit Rate (item rate) contract, payment is based on actual measured quantities of work executed at site, multiplied by agreed unit rates.

q: 31. The action or behavior of an individual in a particular society is concerned with right or wrong; good or bad is
explain: Ethics is defined as the study of the rightness or wrongness, goodness or badness, of an individual's actions and behavior in society.

q: 32. Factors affecting the Morale of the profession is?
explain: Professional morale is influenced by multiple factors including salary/compensation, social norms and respect, and the proper implementation of laws and regulations.

q: 33. The employer has to take responsibility for the wrong of his employees even though he has not committed that mistake is
explain: This is the legal principle of vicarious liability, where an employer is held responsible for the wrongful acts of employees committed in the course of their employment.

q: 34. Quality control ensures that the physical works conforms to
options: Strength specified in the contract document
Standard specified in the contract document
explain: Quality control primarily ensures that the constructed works meet the standards and specifications laid down in the contract document.

q: 35. In Nepal, Public Procurement Act (PPA), was established in
explain: The Public Procurement Act (PPA) of Nepal was enacted in 2063 B.S.

q: 36. Civil Service Act, Nepal was effective from
explain: The Civil Service Act of Nepal became effective from 2038 B.S.

q: 37. In which year (B.S) was the Nepal Engineering Act promulgated?
explain: The Nepal Engineering Council Act was promulgated in 2055 B.S., establishing NEC as an autonomous regulatory body.

q: 38. The registered engineers in Nepal Engineering council should have to renew registration in:
explain: NEC registration renewal does not follow a fixed 1/2/4-year cycle under the given options; the actual renewal requirement differs, so 'none of the above' is correct as per the answer key.

q: 39. Engineers shall not disclose, without ........ confidential information coming the business affairs of technical process of any present or former or employer, or public body on which they serve.
explain: The Code of Ethics requires engineers not to disclose confidential business or technical information without the consent of the employer or client.

q: 40. Which of the following category of engineer is not mentioned in engineering Council rule, 2057 for registration?
explain: The NEC Rule 2057 recognizes categories such as General, Professional, and Non-Nepali Registered Engineer, but does not include 'Chartered Engineer' as a registration category.

q: 41. Engineers shall build their professional reputation on the ......of their services and shall not complete unfairly with others.
explain: The Code of Ethics states engineers should build their professional reputation on the basis (merit) of their services, avoiding unfair competition; per the answer key the intended answer is 'basis'.

q: 42. In general, Nepal Engineering Council meeting per year should be held:
explain: As per NEC rules, the Council is required to hold its general meeting four times a year.

q: 43. Engineers shall act in such a manner as to uphold and enhance the honor, and dignity of the engineering profession and shall act with ....... for bribery, fraud, and corruption.
explain: The Code of Ethics mandates that engineers act with zero tolerance towards bribery, fraud, and corruption to uphold professional integrity.

q: 44. What is the provision in Engineer Council Act and Regulation in Nepal for the punishment if a person practices Engineering work without registering into the Nepal Engineering Council?
options: Rs. 3, 000 fine or imprisonment of 3 months or both
Rs. 1, 000 fine or imprisonment of 1 month or both
explain: Under NEC Act provisions, practicing engineering without registration can attract a fine of Rs. 3,000 or imprisonment up to 3 months, or both.

q: 45. Membership categorized by Nepal Engineering Council for registration is
explain: NEC categorizes registered members as General Engineer, Professional Engineer, and Non-Nepali Registered Engineer; 'Professional Engineer' is the correct categorized membership among the options.

q: 46. The decision of the Nepal Engineering Council meeting minute is authenticated by
explain: The minutes of NEC meetings are authenticated by the Member Secretary of the Council.

q: 47. Ethics is the science of
explain: Ethics is described both as the science of highest positive conduct and as the science of morality, so both apply.

q: 48. Engineers shall build their professional reputation on the ..... of their services and shall not compete unfairly with others
explain: As per the Code of Ethics, professional reputation should be built on the basis of the quality/merit of services rendered, not unfair competition.

q: 49. NEC is an autonomous body as per NEC Act
explain: Nepal Engineering Council was established as an autonomous body under the NEC Act, 2055 B.S.

q: 50. The action or behaviour of an individual in a particular society is concerned with right or wrong, good or bad is
explain: Ethics deals with judging an individual's actions and behavior in society as right or wrong, good or bad.
